questions.question: If a die-roll variable has PMF $1/6$ at each value $1,\ldots,6$, what is $P(X\in\{1,2\})$?
Which condition is exactly the definition of a discrete random variable $X$, necessary as well as sufficient?
options: $X(\omega)$ is an integer for every outcome $\omega$
$X$ takes only finitely many different values
$\mathbb{P}(X\in D)=1$ for some countable set $D$
Each possible value of $X$ has the same probability

questions.question: Let $X$ take the values $1,\tfrac{1}{2},\tfrac{1}{3},\ldots$ with $\mathbb{P}(X=\tfrac{1}{n})=2^{-n}$ for $n=1,2,3,\ldots$. Is $X$ discrete?
options: Yes: all its probability lies on a countable set
No: its values are not integers
No: its values crowd together near $0$ with no gaps
No: it takes infinitely many different values

questions.question: Discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ satisfy $p_X(x)=p_Y(x)$ for every real $x$. What follows?
options: $\mathbb{P}(X\in A)=\mathbb{P}(Y\in A)$ for every set $A$
$X(\omega)=Y(\omega)$ for every outcome $\omega$
$\mathbb{P}(X\in A)=\mathbb{P}(Y\in A)$ only for finite sets $A$
Their means agree, but their distributions may differ

questions.question: A discrete random variable $X$ has $p_X(0)=0.2$, $p_X(1)=0.5$ and $p_X(3)=0.3$. What is $\mathbb{P}(X\le 2.5)$?
Which property of a random variable $X$ rules out that $X$ is discrete?
options: $\mathbb{P}(X=x)=0$ for every real number $x$
$X$ takes countably infinitely many values, with total probability $1$
The values with positive probability include a non-integer such as $0.5$
The positive masses $\mathbb{P}(X=x)$ are not all equal

questions.question: A fair coin is tossed until the first head appears, and $X$ is the number of tosses. Is $X$ discrete?
options: Yes: its values $1,2,3,\ldots$ form a countable set
No: it has infinitely many possible values
No: its masses $\tfrac{1}{2},\tfrac{1}{4},\tfrac{1}{8},\ldots$ never add up to $1$
No: it has no largest value, so it is unbounded

questions.question: A machine is found working with probability $\frac{1}{2}$, and then $X=0$. Otherwise $X$ is its exactly measured repair time in hours, with $\mathbb{P}(X=x)=0$ for every $x\ne0$. Is $X$ a discrete random variable?
options: No: the point masses of $X$ add up to only $\frac{1}{2}$, so no countable set has probability $1$.
Yes: the point mass $\mathbb{P}(X=0)=\frac{1}{2}>0$ is enough to make $X$ discrete.
Yes: the set $\{0\}\cup(0,\infty)$ of possible values has probability $1$.
Yes: $\mathbb{P}(X=x)$ is defined for every real $x$, so $X$ has a mass function and is therefore discrete.
